items.title: Targets: 2025 mostly met, 2026 set as a range
items.text: Only CPI missed in 2025. The 2026 growth target is 4.5% to 5%, and domestic demand leads the ten tasks.

items.title: 15th Plan: no growth figure, carbon first
items.text: No five-year GDP figure. Carbon intensity down 17% over five years, and new welfare targets such as nursing beds.

items.title: This year: growth in range, investment weak
items.text: GDP grew 4.7% in H1. Jan–Aug fixed-asset investment −7.2%, and PPI turned positive at +2.0%.

items.title: For us: follow the policy money and the rules
items.text: Watch services spending and equipment support, do the carbon sums early, protect exports.

notes: Four takeaways. First, targets: 2025 hit its main goals except consumer prices, and 2026 sets the growth target as a range for the first time, with building a strong domestic market as the first of ten tasks. Second, the 15th Five-Year Plan sets no five-year GDP figure, makes carbon rather than energy use the main green yardstick, and adds welfare targets such as nursing beds in elderly care homes and childcare enrolment. Third, delivery this year: growth sits inside the range, but investment and retail sales are weak while factory prices have turned up. Data run to August, and Q3 GDP comes out on October 19. Fourth, what it means for us, which the last page turns into three actions.
